usage: policy for libraries directly referenced in code that need updating
name: Open source directly referenced in code should be kept up to date
description: Utilizing libraries that are out of date may mean that fixes and improvements to the library are not being leveraged in your companies code.
detailedDescription: Open source libraries are continuously being updated and improved. Newer versions can quite often have security fixes and new vulnerabilities. This is why it is critical to periodically update your dependencies.

args.name: compareMajorVersion
args.label: Compare
args.tooltip: When major version selected there will be no violation if the latest version of a library is just a minor version change.

args.name: numberOfVersionsToSkip
args.label: Major Version Drift
args.tooltip: A violation will occur only if the difference between the latest major version and the deployed major version is more than or equal to the drift.

args.name: daysCheck
args.label: Days since update
args.tooltip: Days that a library that has a newer version can remain without being updated.
